amazing-grace.text: These words were first printed in 1779, in Olney Hymns, a hymnbook made in an English village with the poet William Cowper. Their title there was Faith's Review and Expectation.
The tune uses only five different notes, a pentatonic scale. Moved to F sharp major, all five are black keys on a piano.
amazing-grace.source: The tune's own notes (G, A, B, D and E)

amazing-grace.text: The tune, now called New Britain, survives from 1828 on the back of a letter, and was printed in 1829 in Columbian Harmony, a shape-note book whose notes have shapes that show their place in the scale.

The verse about ten thousand years, often sung last, isn't from the 1779 words: it comes from a 1790 hymn collection. Harriet Beecher Stowe printed it with Amazing Grace in Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852), and no hymnal paired them until 1909.
